actor: mk — solo gardener of a ~98-project, agent-heavy, terminal-native estate
trigger: Sitting down at the machine (morning, or returning after hours away) with agents having run on wall-clock the whole time: 'what moved while I was gone, and what waits on me?'

steps.step: Open Autarch and arrive to orientation, not obligation: a catch-up reading of what moved since the last visit, before anything asks for a decision
build_surface: catch-up briefing pane (new — the Empire Timeline / begin-from-stillness steal)

steps.step: Scan the estate — pivoted by container (ecosystems → projects) or by theme: rows quiet unless attention-worthy — verdict column, card fractions, live session counts, themes with live salons; visibility is opt-in at this scale, not opt-out
Read the waiting-on-me axis: which agents are blocked on a human right now, distinguished from working and from dead
build_surface: tmux capture-pane scrape (Claude-Squad pattern: prompt-scrape + content hash)

steps.step: Notice cross-garden signals routed by the layer structure — most arrive toast-class; a cross-layer contradiction (fast probe vs slow doctrine) earns popup-class
build_surface: CanonGraph layer/serving graph (read-only, third data source)

steps.step: Choose where attention lands: enter a garden (tmux switch-client) or a theme's salon, or close Autarch owing nothing

mental_model: The walk is the watching/waiting half of the gardening loop — 'lots of context switching and deep diving and then watching/waiting for intervention points.' Stellaris gets stillness free by freezing the world; mk's world never halts, so the door must stop *the gardener* instead: orientation completes before any obligation is allowed to speak. The estate is scanned like an outliner, not read like an inbox — at ~98 projects the default is quiet, and a row earns its place on the walk. Leaving without acting is a successful walk, not an aborted one.

closed_decisions: The door transcribes card-check, tmux, and the layer graph; it owns no state (HUD ruling, ratified via the vision statement — the Mayor lost its data 22 times being a world instead of an overlay)
Orientation-before-obligation is the pause-steal: nothing demands a decision until the catch-up read is done
At estate scale the default is quiet-unless-attention-worthy (Stellaris C / show_in_outliner + the interrupt-fatigue resentment)

closed_decisions.decision: Waiting-on-me detection comes from tmux scraping (Claude-Squad pattern), not a herdr migration

open_questions.question: What does the catch-up briefing read from — tmux history, cass session archives, git log since last visit, or a per-repo events ledger?
Does the walk open on the briefing with NO list (provocation 1 from the Stellaris teardown) or on the briefing above the ranked rows?
How fresh must cross-garden signals be — computed on door open, or by a background cadence?

mk corrected the axis framing: the standing threads are scaffolding, not preference ('the reason i work in sessions/threads is because we haven't built autarch/garden salon'), so the row stays the garden and the question becomes decomposition order — which thread-compensated function does the walk absorb first: the catch-up briefing (exercised daily via companion threads) or the waiting-on-me triage? And does the door render live threads transitionally, as scaffolding on the way down?

implied_features: Catch-up briefing on door open (what moved since last visit, per garden, newest-first)
Waiting-on-me column driven by tmux prompt-scraping with working/waiting/dead states
Delivery classes (off/toast/popup) for row-level and cross-garden signals, config in door.yaml
Visibility opt-in at scale: rows collapse to quiet by default, attention-worthiness promotes them

reference_lineage.what_it_shaped: Pairs A (orientation-before-obligation), C (outliner / show_in_outliner quiet default), G (Empire Timeline as the park/load bridge)
The human as the top of an escalation ladder, not a notification target — pre-triaged severity routing shapes what may interrupt the walk
Ambient Governance and Continuous Reading — health visible without demanding; signals, not threshold alarms

reference_lineage.app: Digital gardens — Appleton's ethos, Komoroske's compendium
reference_lineage.what_it_shaped: Named by mk at validation, not torn down: 'it seems like all of the above CUJs are a Komoroske/Appleton-style version of product management + gardening/tending' — the walk as tending a topography, not clearing a timeline

evidence.quote: stellaris and other paradox games seem like a natural fit; lots of context switching and deep diving and then watching/waiting for intervention points
evidence.assumption_tested: That the door's job is task management — it is not; it is attention routing between watching and diving

evidence.quote: I think Autarch should be the UI/HUD/way for humans to play in/build/grow the garden of their projects/interests (especially when they are so deeply interrelated via pace layers/systems like my projects are).
evidence.assumption_tested: That Autarch is an app that owns workflow — the HUD ruling makes it an overlay that transcribes

evidence.quote: hmm check my sessions to determine how I actually work
evidence.assumption_tested: That the walk scans gardens — observed August behavior: 24/31 active days, median 3 real sessions across 2 projects, ~40 fleet one-shots/day, two-thirds of the estate dormant in any month (quiet-default confirmed)

evidence.quote: well, the reason i work in sessions/threads is because we haven't built autarch/garden salon
evidence.assumption_tested: That standing threads are revealed preference — mk ruled them a workaround for the unbuilt estate; the daily companion threads are the hand-rolled version of this CUJ's briefing, which makes the briefing the walk's most-exercised missing organ

evidence.quote: it seems like all of the above CUJs are a Komoroske/Appleton-style version of product management + gardening/tending
evidence.assumption_tested: That the derived journeys needed correction before they were mk's — all four validated as walked, with the batched edits; the lineage mk named locates the whole set in the digital-gardening tradition

success_condition: mk opens the door after a day away and, within about a minute, knows what moved and what waits on them — then either dives or closes it without guilt, and recognizes the walk as the Stellaris loop they described rather than an inbox they were assigned.
